entries.title: Neurons & complex systems
entries.summary: I took the EPFL/Blue Brain Simulation Neuroscience MOOC from September to around December 2024, then began my own experiments. The simulator has been rewritten repeatedly as its underlying model changed.

source.note: The author began the Simulation Neuroscience MOOC in September 2024 and finished around December 2024. He then started his own experimental work, including major rewrites and changes in modeling paradigm. The wish to build a realistic virtual intelligence and simulation existed earlier; September 2024 dates his neuroscience studies, not the origin of that ambition. Current technical research is unpublished.

entries.title: Artificial agents
entries.when: Artificial societies: philosophical work since early 2025; applied research since March 2026
entries.summary: I have been studying how memory and interactions shape consistent simulated societies. My conceptual work developed around early 2025; since March 2026 I have been actively testing hypotheses in code, with mLearn as one experimental environment.

source.note: The author’s interest in artificial societies is a childhood dream, not a result of Kodu or the neuroscience MOOC. Focused philosophical research began early 2025 (approximate). March 2026 marks the start of an ongoing applied-research stage with coded experiments using mLearn; that stage is not a single finished event.

phases.note: Conceptual research into consistent simulations, memory and interacting agents.

phases.when: Since March 2026 · applied research and ongoing coded experiments
phases.note: Direct experiments testing agent/simulation hypotheses in an educational environment with mLearn; this is still being developed.

entries.title: Voxel rendering
entries.when: Computer graphics experiments since April 2025 · ongoing
entries.summary: Ongoing graphics experiments across several renderer implementations and rewrites: voxel ray traversal, reflection and refraction, spatial acceleration and path tracing. My first voxel tutorial port needed its x86 SIMD code adapted to ARM NEON on the Mac.

source.note: The author recovered a video establishing April 2025 as the start of systematic graphics learning. June 2025 recordings on the 9th and 13th are surviving renderer recording dates, not the start. Rendering and ray tracing experiments are still ongoing, with repeated template changes/rebuilds. An initial project used Jacco Bikker’s Ray Tracing with Voxels in C++ tutorial (published April 2024); the author and AI agents adapted its x86 SIMD acceleration to ARM NEON for macOS. Distinguish reused tutorial/template from author-owned algorithms and modifications.
